mainTopic: Whether the doubled wording in the deal with בני גד ובני ראובן teaches the rule of תנאי כפול (a doubled condition), as רבי מאיר holds, or is needed for its own content, as רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי מאיר's source for תנאי כפול: the words 'בארץ כנען' seem extra, so they teach that a condition must be stated both ways. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל answers that those words are needed. Without them, we would think בני גד ובני ראובן get a share only in ארץ גלעד. The גמרא then gives רבי מאיר's answer: 'בתוככם' already means everywhere. A ברייתא brings רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's parable of a father dividing fields among his sons. In the parable, the doubled wording gives the son a share of the rest of the property. The גמרא asks why this parable does not match the משנה, and answers that the two were said before and after רבי מאיר's challenge. Next, the גמרא tests רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view against פסוקים that state both sides of a condition: קין, אברהם and אליעזר, בחוקותי, and ישעיהו. Each time it shows that the second half teaches something new. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a question about a phrase in the ישעיהו פסוק, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the extra words teach the doubled condition
steps.stepSummary: Explaining רבי מאיר's view, the גמרא asks why the פסוק needs the words 'בארץ כנען' and concludes that they come to teach תנאי כפול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need [the words 'in the land of Canaan']? Learn from this that they come to teach the rule of a doubled condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא, explaining רבי מאיר's source, points to words in the פסוק that seem unnecessary and uses them as proof that a condition must be stated both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse already says 'ונאחזו בתוככם', meaning they will get land among you, so 'בארץ כנען' seems to add nothing new. An extra phrase in a פסוק must teach something. רבי מאיר says it teaches that every condition must be doubled (תנאי כפול).

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? Used to point out wording that seems extra
Learn from this; conclude from it
A doubled condition, stating both what happens if it is kept and what happens if it is not

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for רבי מאיר's rule that a condition only works if both sides are spelled out. That rule matters for conditions in קידושין, גיטין and other deals.

phrases.english: Why do I need [this]?
phrases.notes: He means the words 'בארץ כנען' at the end of במדבר 32:30, quoted just before this line.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לִתְנַאי כָּפוּל הוּא דַּאֲתָא.
phrases.english: Learn from it that it comes for a doubled condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי מאיר's reading of the פסוק about בני גד ובני ראובן, which began earlier on the daf.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a condition must be doubled (תנאי כפול)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra words 'בארץ כנען' in במדבר 32:30

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: the words are needed for their own meaning
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says 'בארץ כנען' is not extra. Without it, we would think בני גד ובני ראובן inherit only in ארץ גלעד and not in ארץ כנען at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says: If the תורה had not written 'in the land of Canaan,' I would have said that 'they shall get a possession among you' means in ארץ גלעד. But in ארץ כנען, they would get nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל pushes back on רבי מאיר's proof. He shows that the words 'בארץ כנען' have their own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof from an 'extra' phrase only works if the phrase is truly extra. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says it is not: 'בתוככם' alone could be read as a share in ארץ גלעד, the land on the east side. 'בארץ כנען' is needed to tell us they would get a share in the Land itself, so nothing is left over to teach תנאי כפול.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
I would have said; the mistaken idea we would have had
They shall get a possession among you
The land east of the ירדן that בני גד ובני ראובן asked for

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says:
If the Merciful One had not written 'in the land of Canaan,'
I would have said that 'they shall get a possession among you' means:
in the land of Gilead,
but in the land of Canaan, not at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אָמַר: אִי לָא כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's claim that 'בארץ כנען' is extra.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the extra words in step 1, not any other source.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words are not extra. They are needed to show that בני גד ובני ראובן would inherit in ארץ כנען and not only in ארץ גלעד.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's answer: 'among you' already means everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר would respond and answers that, for him, 'בתוככם' already means any place you own, including ארץ כנען.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? [He holds that] 'among you' means anywhere that you have [land].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי מאיר against רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the word 'בתוככם' on its own already includes ארץ כנען, so there was never a risk of reading it as only ארץ גלעד. That means 'בארץ כנען' really is extra. It is free to teach תנאי כפול, and his proof stands.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir [how does he answer this]?
'Among you' means any place that you have.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's rejection on behalf of רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of a word: 'בתוככם' already includes ארץ כנען.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בארץ כנען' is needed so that we don't limit 'בתוככם' to ארץ גלעד.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בתוככם' already covers every place, so 'בארץ כנען' is extra and teaches תנאי כפול.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's parable of the father and his sons
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a parable from רבי חנינא בן גמליאל. A father gives each son a field, but one son gets his field only if he pays two hundred זוז. If that son doesn't pay, he shares the rest of the property with his brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל said: Here is a parable. What is this like? It is like a person who was dividing his property among his sons. He said: My son so-and-so will inherit such-and-such field, and my son so-and-so will inherit such-and-such field, and my son so-and-so will pay two hundred זוז and inherit such-and-such field. And if he does not pay, he will inherit with his brothers in the rest of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parable that backs up רבי חנינא בן גמליאל. It sets up the point that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father states both sides for the third son: pay and get this field, or don't pay and share the rest. This is just like בני גד ובני ראובן, who get ארץ גלעד if they fight, or a share in ארץ כנען if they don't. The parable is building toward the question of why the father needed to say the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel said:
A parable: to what is this matter similar?
To a person who was dividing his property among his sons.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: פְּלוֹנִי בְּנִי יִירַשׁ שָׂדֶה פְּלוֹנִית,
phrases.english: He said: My son so-and-so will inherit such-and-such field,
and my son so-and-so will inherit such-and-such field,
and my son so-and-so will give two hundred zuz
and inherit such-and-such field,
and if he does not give,
he will inherit with his brothers in the rest of the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מָשָׁל לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's side of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deal with בני גד ובני ראובן is like a father who gives one son a field for payment, and otherwise lets him share the rest of the property.

steps.title: The doubled wording is what gives the son his share
steps.stepSummary: Only the father's doubled wording lets the son share the rest of the property. In the same way, the doubled wording in the פסוק is needed to give בני גד ובני ראובן a share in ארץ כנען.
steps.simpleTranslation: What caused him to inherit with his brothers in the rest of the property? His doubling [of the condition] caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: The parable reaches its point: the second half of the father's words had a real job of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the words 'if he does not pay, he shares the rest,' the son who did not pay would get nothing at all. So the doubled wording was needed for its own content, not to make the condition valid. In the same way, the second half of the deal with בני גד ובני ראובן gives them land in ארץ כנען and does not prove a general rule of תנאי כפול.

keyTerms.meaning: His doubling; the second half of the condition

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the extra words 'בארץ כנען' teach that every condition must be doubled. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: those words are needed to give בני גד ובני ראובן land in ארץ כנען. Like the father in the parable, the doubled wording has its own content and does not teach a general rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'his doubling caused it' as support for רבי מאיר. The point is that the doubling did something specific, giving a share in the rest of the property. It was not needed to make the condition work.

phrases.english: Who caused him to inherit
with his brothers in the rest of the property?
His doubling caused it for him.
phrases.notes: 'His doubling' means the father spelling out the second side: what happens if the son doesn't pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי גָּרַם לוֹ לִירַשׁ עִם אֶחָיו בִּשְׁאָר נְכָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the parable in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The doubled wording is needed for its own content, giving a share of the rest. So according to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, it does not teach the rule of תנאי כפול.

steps.title: The parable does not match the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה suggests the doubled wording also helps for ארץ גלעד, while the parable suggests the doubling helps only for the rest of the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the parable is not like the משנה! There it says: 'You might think they would not inherit even in ארץ כנען.' So the doubling helps for ארץ גלעד too. And here it says: 'What let him inherit the rest of the property with his brothers? The doubling did.' So the doubling helps only for the rest of the property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the parable from Step 4. It says the parable does not fit what רבי חנינא בן גמליאל said in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אפילו' (even) in the משנה hints that without the doubling, the tribes would surely lose ארץ גלעד as well. That makes the doubling necessary for גלעד too. In the parable, though, the son gets the conditional field (which stands for גלעד) no matter what, and the doubling only gives him a share in the rest (which stands for ארץ כנען).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not similar, it doesn't match
Doubling, saying a condition both ways (if yes, if not)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the matching straight. The son's conditional field stands for ארץ גלעד, and 'the rest of the property' stands for ארץ כנען.

phrases.english: But the parable is not similar to the Mishnah!
There it teaches:
phrases.notes: 'There' means our משנה, in the words of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: It could have been understood that even
in the land of Canaan they would not inherit,
phrases.notes: 'Even' hints that they would surely not get ארץ גלעד either.

phrases.english: this shows that the doubling, for the land of Gilead,
is also effective.
And here it teaches:
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ברייתא with the parable from Step 4.

phrases.english: What caused him to inherit
with his brothers in the rest of the property?
His doubling caused him,
this shows that the doubling, for the rest of the property,
is what it is effective for!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the parable brought in Steps 4-5 by comparing it to the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The parable of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה the doubling is needed for both גלעד and כנען, but in the parable it is needed only for the rest of the property (כנען). So the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: Before and after רבי מאיר's challenge
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reflects what רבי חנינא בן גמליאל held before רבי מאיר challenged him with 'ונאחזו', and the parable reflects what he held after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one was said before רבי מאיר said to him 'ונאחזו'. That one was said after רבי מאיר said to him 'ונאחזו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. It says רבי חנינא בן גמליאל said the two things at two different stages of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, in the משנה, רבי חנינא בן גמליאל held that without the doubling the tribes would lose גלעד too. רבי מאיר then argued that 'ונאחזו בתוככם' already gives them ארץ כנען. Afterward, רבי חנינא בן גמליאל explained that without 'בארץ כנען' we would read that phrase as referring to גלעד, which means they would get גלעד anyway, exactly like the son's conditional field in the parable.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no contradiction
'And they shall take possession', the word רבי מאיר used to challenge

steps.whatToRemember: The two statements of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל belong to two stages. Before רבי מאיר's challenge, the doubling was needed even for גלעד. After it, the doubling was needed only for ארץ כנען, just like the parable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא reading a debate as a conversation that moves along, where one side can change his position in response to the other.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
This one was before he said to him,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the משנה's statement with the word 'even'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir, 'and they shall take possession',
that one was after he said to him,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the parable in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir, 'and they shall take possession'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא. הָא מִקַּמֵּי דְּנֵימָא לֵיהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְנֹאחֲזוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time: two stages of the same debate
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the parable seem to give two different roles to the doubling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before רבי מאיר's challenge, רבי חנינא בן גמליאל needed the doubling even for גלעד. After the challenge, he agreed the tribes get גלעד anyway, so the doubling only gives ארץ כנען, matching the parable.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק about קין state both sides?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק to קין spells out both the 'if you do well' and the 'if you do not do well' sides. That fits רבי מאיר, but why would רבי חנינא need it?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי מאיר. That is why the פסוק says: 'If you do well, it will be lifted up, and if you do not do well, sin crouches at the door.' But according to רבי חנינא, why do we need both sides?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא בן גמליאל with a פסוק that states both sides of a condition. For רבי מאיר, this doubled wording is exactly what we expect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that every condition must be stated both ways, so the doubled wording in the warning to קין fits his view. רבי חנינא holds that the positive side already implies the negative side. So for him, the second half of the פסוק seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works well (for one opinion, but not the other)
A doubled condition, stated both ways

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir,
this is why it is written:
"If you do well, it will be lifted up,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא תֵיטִיב לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ״.
phrases.english: and if you do not do well, sin crouches at the door."
But according to Rabbi Chanina, why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the parable to testing רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view against other פסוקים
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view that a condition does not need to be doubled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the positive side already implies the negative side, the פסוק's negative half seems extra.

steps.title: The second half teaches that there is punishment
steps.stepSummary: Without the second half, we might think that failing brings no reward and also no punishment. The פסוק teaches that there is punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: if you do well, you get a reward, and if you do not do well, you get no reward but also no punishment. The פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי חנינא. The second half of the פסוק is not just the other side of the condition; it adds new information.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first half alone, the opposite of 'reward' would only be 'no reward.' The second half, 'sin crouches at the door,' adds that there is actual punishment. So the words are needed even for someone who does not require a תנאי כפול.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
It teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
if you do well, a reward;

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא תֵיטִיב – לָא אַגְרָא וְלָא דִּינָא,
phrases.english: if you do not do well, neither reward nor punishment;
so it teaches us.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra words teach new content, so they are not just a doubled condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Failing to do well would bring no reward but also no punishment
steps.terutzMaskana: Failing to do well brings actual punishment

steps.title: Why does אברהם release אליעזר from the oath outright?
steps.stepSummary: אברהם tells אליעזר he will be free of the oath if they will not give her to him. That fits רבי מאיר, but why would רבי חנינא בן גמליאל need it?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי מאיר. That is why the פסוק says: 'Then you shall be clear from my oath.' But according to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, why do we need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that spells out the negative side of a condition and asks the same question for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם made אליעזר swear to bring a wife for יצחק, and then also stated the other side: if they refuse, he is free. For רבי מאיר that doubling is required. For רבי חנינא, the first instruction should already imply the release.

keyTerms.meaning: This is why it is written

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir,
this is why it is written: "Then you shall be clear from my oath,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:41. The פסוק goes on: 'if they will not give her to you.'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel, why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: ״אָז תִּנָּקֶה מֵאָלָתִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge as step 8, now with a second פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view that a condition does not need to be doubled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The release from the oath is just the negative side of the condition, so it should not need to be said.

steps.title: Without the release, he might have to bring her against her family's wishes
steps.stepSummary: The release is needed. Otherwise we might think that if she wants to come but her family does not, אליעזר must bring her anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: where she agrees but they (her family) do not, he must bring her against their will. The פסוק teaches us that he does not have to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the release teaches something new: אליעזר does not have to take her if her family objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case here is one where the girl is willing but her family is not. Without the release, we might think the oath still forces אליעזר to bring her over their objection. The פסוק tells us he is free in that case.

phrases.english: It was needed; it would enter your mind to say:
where it is acceptable to her
but not acceptable to them,
he should bring her against their will;
so it teaches us.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra words cover a specific case that we would have gotten wrong
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If she agrees but her family does not, אליעזר must still bring her
steps.terutzMaskana: He is released from the oath and does not bring her against her family's will

steps.title: Why the extra words 'if the woman is not willing'?
steps.stepSummary: A different פסוק in the same story says 'if the woman is not willing.' The גמרא asks why that clause is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the words 'If the woman is not willing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges another phrase in the same story. It seems extra, especially for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that אליעזר is free if the family refuses. Now the גמרא asks what the clause about the woman herself refusing adds.

phrases.english: "If the woman is not willing" — why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the same kind of challenge on a parallel clause in the story
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause 'if the woman is not willing'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The negative side of the condition seems extra, and the family-refusal case is already covered.

steps.title: Without it, he might have to bring her against her own will
steps.stepSummary: The clause is needed. Otherwise we might think that if the family agrees but she does not, אליעזר must bring her anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: where they (her family) agree but she does not, he must bring her against her will. The פסוק teaches us that he does not have to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this clause covers the opposite case from step 11: the family agrees, but the woman refuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each release clause covers a different case. One covers the family refusing, and this one covers the woman refusing. So neither is extra, and both fit רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view as well.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, every פסוק that seems to spell out a doubled condition actually teaches something new: punishment for קין, and freedom for אליעזר whether the family refuses or the woman refuses.

phrases.english: It was needed; it would enter your mind to say:
where it is acceptable to them
but not acceptable to her,
he should bring her against her will;
so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 and mirrors the answer in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra words cover a specific case that we would have gotten wrong
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the family agrees but she does not, אליעזר must still bring her
steps.terutzMaskana: He is released and does not bring her against her own will

steps.title: Why does בחוקותי spell out both blessing and curse?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים in בחוקותי state both sides: walk in My statutes, or reject them. This fits רבי מאיר, but why would רבי חנינא בן גמליאל need both?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי מאיר, this is why the תורה writes both 'If you walk in My statutes' and 'And if you reject My statutes.' But according to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, why do I need both?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another example of a double condition, the blessings and curses in בחוקותי. It asks why רבי חנינא בן גמליאל would need the Torah to say both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that every condition must state both sides, so the double wording in בחוקותי is exactly what he expects. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds that the second side is understood on its own. So for him, writing 'if you reject' looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works fine (for one opinion)
This is why it is written
My statutes; the name of the section of blessings and curses

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir,
this is why it is written:
"If you walk in My statutes,"
"And if you reject My statutes,"
but according to Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same challenge pattern from steps 8 and 10, now with a new pair of פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל that a double condition is not needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the second side is understood on its own, the תורה should not need to write 'if you reject My statutes'.

steps.title: Without the second half we might think rejecting brings no curse
steps.stepSummary: The second half is needed. Otherwise we might think that keeping the statutes brings blessing, while rejecting them brings nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: 'If you walk in My statutes' brings blessing, but 'if you reject My statutes' brings neither blessing nor curse. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second פסוק is not there to make a double condition. It is there to teach that rejecting the statutes brings an actual curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first פסוק alone, we would only learn that if you do not keep the statutes, you lose the blessing. There would be a middle option of nothing happening. The second פסוק rules out that middle option and adds active punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)

phrases.english: It is needed,
for it would enter your mind to say:
"If you walk in My statutes" means blessing,
"If you reject My statutes" means
neither blessing nor curse,
so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: It teaches us that rejecting brings a real curse, not just losing the blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 using the same reasoning as step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second clause has its own purpose (teaches active punishment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rejecting the statutes would bring neither blessing nor curse.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rejecting the statutes brings a curse, so the second פסוק is needed even for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Why does ישעיהו spell out both obeying and refusing?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים in ישעיהו say 'if you are willing and obey' and also 'if you refuse and rebel.' This fits רבי מאיר, but why would רבי חנינא בן גמליאל need both?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי מאיר, this is why it is written 'If you are willing and obey...' and also 'And if you refuse and rebel...' But according to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, why do I need both?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more double condition, this time from ישעיהו. It asks the same question: why would רבי חנינא בן גמליאל need both sides written?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, both sides are spelled out. That matches רבי מאיר's rule. For רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, the 'refuse and rebel' half seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the פסוק (abbreviated וְגוֹ׳)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir,
this is why it is written
"If you are willing and obey, etc.,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:19. The rest of the פסוק says you will eat the good of the land.

phrases.english: "And if you refuse and rebel, etc.,"
but according to Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same challenge again, with a new pair of פסוקים from ישעיהו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל that a double condition is not needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the opposite side is understood on its own, 'if you refuse and rebel' should be extra.

steps.title: Without the second half we might think refusing brings no harm
steps.stepSummary: The second half is needed. Otherwise we might think obeying brings good, while refusing brings neither good nor bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: 'If you are willing' brings good, but 'if you refuse' brings neither good nor bad. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as before. The second פסוק teaches that refusing brings real harm, not just a missed reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'if you refuse,' we would think the only result of not obeying is losing the good. The פסוק adds that the one who rebels is actually punished. So the extra half has its own lesson, even for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.whatToRemember: In all these cases (קין, אברהם and אליעזר, בחוקותי, ישעיהו), the גמרא shows that the second half of a double condition can teach something new. So these פסוקים fit רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view too, and do not force רבי מאיר's rule.

phrases.english: It is needed,
for it would enter your mind to say:
"If you are willing" means good,
"And if you refuse" means
neither good nor bad,
so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 the same way step 15 answered step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second clause has its own purpose (teaches active punishment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Refusing would bring neither good nor bad.
steps.terutzMaskana: Refusing brings harm, so the second פסוק is needed even for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Opening a new question about the פסוק in ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins asking 'What...', starting a question about the meaning of a phrase in the ישעיהו פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: This single word is only a setup. The גמרא is starting a new question about the meaning of a phrase in the פסוק from ישעיהו, and the question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument about double conditions is finished. Since the גמרא just quoted ישעיהו, it now turns to explain a phrase from that פסוק. This is a side discussion that grows out of the quote.

phrases.english: What...
phrases.notes: The question breaks off here and picks up on the next amud, asking about a phrase in the ישעיהו פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new side question about the ישעיהו פסוק quoted in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of a phrase in the ישעיהו פסוק (the question continues on the next amud).
